options: The number of positive elements in nums
The sum of the positive elements
A new array of the positives
explanation: `filter` keeps elements matching the predicate; `count` returns how many survived (as a `long`). To sum them instead you'd end with `.sum()`.

title: Recall: aggregate an int[]
prompt: Fill in the stream aggregation operations.
explanation: `Arrays.stream(nums)` opens an IntStream; `sum`/`max` aggregate, `filter` narrows before you count or sum.

title: Drill: sum of positives (streams)
prompt: From memory: return the sum of the positive numbers in `nums` using a stream — `Arrays.stream(...).filter(...).sum()`.

solution.explanation: `filter` passes along only elements matching the predicate, and `IntStream.sum()` returns 0 for an empty stream, so no special cases are needed. O(n).

hints: Three steps: open a stream over the array, keep only positives, total them.
`Arrays.stream(nums)` gives an IntStream; chain `.filter(x -> x > 0)` then `.sum()`.

title: Recall: int[] ↔ List<Integer>
code:
int[] arr = list.stream().{{1}}(i -> i).toArray();          // List -> int[]
List<Integer> boxed = Arrays.stream(nums).{{2}}().collect(Collectors.toList()); // int[] -> List
explanation: `mapToInt(i -> i)` unboxes Integer→int for `toArray`; `boxed()` boxes int→Integer so `collect(Collectors.toList())` can build a `List<Integer>`.

title: Drill: int[] to List<Integer>
prompt: From memory: convert `nums` to a `List<Integer>` in one line using `Arrays.stream(...).boxed().collect(...)`.

solution.explanation: `boxed()` turns the IntStream into a `Stream<Integer>`, which `Collectors.toList()` can gather into a `List<Integer>`. O(n).

hints: An IntStream holds primitives, but a List needs Integer objects. Box first.
